content: coffee A blast during a film shoot near London’s O2 arena ignited a fire that consumed a van and badly damaged a car and a lorry. Fire crews were summoned to an open‑air yard on Dock Road in Silvertown just before eight o’clock on Saturday. After roughly an hour, with twenty‑five firefighters on the scene, the flames were brought under control and no injuries were reported. Authorities said the blaze originated from a pre‑arranged filming activity close to the venue, which is slated to host shows by Niall Horan and Texas next week. The London Fire Brigade updated on X, noting the fire is now contained, one vehicle was destroyed while most of a car and a lorry suffered damage, and there are no injury reports. They added that the incident followed a controlled explosion on the set that escaped containment, prompting rapid extinguishing efforts; crews will stay until the evening ends. The yard lies near the Thames cable‑car link, and a Metropolitan Police spokesman confirmed they are aware of eyewitness accounts of explosions heard close to the O2 in Greenwich.
